title: Glassbox: Request investigation palette and errormap for payload forensics
creator: Maya Castillo
description: Problem: Operators currently jump between disparate panels to understand why requests fail (logs, traces, raw payloads). This is slow, error-prone, and makes post-incident debugging costly. Goal: design a compact, contextual investigation palette — "Glassbox" — that surfaces an errormap, temporal request timeline, retry lineage, and structured payload diffs in a single, dockable UI. The palette should support fast hypothesis formation, lightweight comparisons across retries, and clear links to rollout/route config and cost impact data. Scope: palette launcher from request row, errormap visualization, timeline scrubber with token-level annotations, retry stack list with inline payload diff, quick actions (replay, copy, open in full inspector), and a lightweight taxonomy legend for error classification. Out of scope for this ticket: backend instrumentation changes for token-level spans (tracked in ENG-92014), deep log ingestion pipeline work.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Glassbox launcher from request list opens right-docked palette with <= 150ms animation
Errormap visualizes frequency and severity across request steps and highlights first-failure frame
Timeline scrubber shows inlined KB/feature-flags and latency spikes; hovering reveals token-level annotations if available
Retry lineage shows up to 5 recent attempts with payload-size and delta badges; clicking diff expands inline structured diff
Quick actions wired to placeholders for replay and open-full-inspector flows
Prototype validated in 3 moderated usability sessions with achievement of task completion rate >= 85% for triage flows
